transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well, hello. I suppose I came in because... well, even on my better days, I just can't seem to shake this feeling that some people are watching me. Mostly at my church and, um, in my Tuesday walking club. Which, by the way, we've had to move our walking route lately because of all that construction over on 4th street. The dust is just terrible for my allergies, and I told Brenda we should walk by the park instead, but she never listens. She bought these neon pink sneakers last week, just entirely too bright for a woman our age if you ask me. 

But anyway... where was I? Oh, right, the people at church and the club. I just know they're putting little messages about me in the Sunday bulletin. Or, you know, hiding things about me in what they say when we're walking or having coffee. It's just very unsettling, and I don't know why they'd do that. I've been going to that church for thirty years, and I always help with the bake sales, so it just doesn't make sense.
How long have you believed that people at church and in your walking club are sending messages about you?

Well, let's see... it's been a while now. I'd say the messages, and the voices, and just having such a hard time keeping my thoughts straight... it's been going on for about eleven months. Which is funny, because eleven months ago was right around the time my sister's cat had kittens. Oh, they were the sweetest little things, mostly orange tabbies, but there was one little black one with white paws that we called Socks. My sister wanted to keep him, but her husband is terribly allergic. He gets these awful hives all over his neck whenever he's near a cat. We tried all sorts of things, even that special shampoo, but nothing worked. So they ended up giving Socks to the neighbor's daughter, who just started middle school. She plays the clarinet, you know. I can hear her practicing sometimes when I sit on my porch. She's getting better, but she still squeaks on the high notes. But yes, about eleven months, I'd say.
Do you hear voices that other people cannot hear?

Well, yes, I suppose I do. Sometimes, especially when the house is just perfectly quiet, I'll hear my name being called. Or just a few words, and it sounds exactly like my friend's voice coming right out of the kitchen, or maybe from out on the porch. It's so clear that I actually answer back before I remember that nobody is even there! I'll call out, "I'm in the living room, Brenda!" But of course, she's not there. 

Speaking of Brenda, she did come over last Tuesday and brought this lemon loaf she baked. She got the recipe from that daytime cooking show, the one with the host who always wears those loud floral aprons. I used to have a beautiful floral apron back in the eighties, but it got a terrible grease stain on it when my husband—God rest his soul—tried to fry a turkey for Thanksgiving. Oh, what an absolute disaster that was. The oil splattered everywhere on the patio, and we ended up having to order Chinese food, and they even forgot the egg rolls! I was so disappointed, because their egg rolls are usually the best part. 

But... oh, what was I saying? Right, the voices. Yes, it's usually just my name or a little greeting when I'm all alone in the house.
Since these experiences began, have they caused a noticeable decline in your ability to manage your usual daily activities, relationships, or responsibilities?

Well, I suppose things have changed a bit. I still live at home, you know, in the same house my husband and I bought back in '78. Oh, the housing market was so different then. We paid next to nothing compared to what these young couples are paying now. The Smith boy down the street just bought a tiny little two-bedroom, and you wouldn't believe what he paid for it. And it doesn't even have a finished basement! Our basement has that lovely wood paneling we put up in the eighties. 

But, um, yes, my daily activities. I have stopped keeping up with my quilting gatherings. And the walking club, well, I just haven't been going as much. And my gardening... I used to have the most beautiful hydrangeas. The secret is the soil acidity, you know. If you want them blue, you have to add aluminum sulfate. My grandmother taught me that. She had a garden that belonged in a magazine. But lately, I just haven't had the energy or the mind for it. 

So my daughter, bless her heart, she's started checking on me more often. She calls to make sure I'm eating my meals and keeping up with my appointments. She's a good girl, works in human resources over at the hospital. Always wearing those sharp little blazers. I tried to sew her a blazer once, but the shoulder pads just never sat quite right. It made her look like a football player! We had such a laugh about that. But yes, she checks on me quite a bit now.
Besides believing that people are watching you and sending you messages, do you have any other unusual beliefs that you feel certain are true?

Well, no, not exactly. It's really just what I told you before. I came in because, even on my better days, I just can't shake that feeling that those people at church and in my walking club are watching me. And they put those little messages about me right in the Sunday bulletin, or they say things that I know are meant for me. 

The Sunday bulletin used to be so nice, you know. Back when Mrs. Higgins was the church secretary, she used to put a little recipe at the bottom of the last page every week. Her pecan pie recipe was just to die for. She used dark corn syrup instead of light, which made all the difference. And she always brought one to the church potluck. Oh, those potlucks were something else. We used to hold them in the old fellowship hall before they renovated it. They put down that new carpet, a sort of teal color, which I never thought was quite right for a church basement. It shows every little crumb, and after the Sunday school kids have their graham crackers, well, it's just a mess. I told the pastor they should have gone with a nice speckled brown, but they didn't listen to me. 

But yes, no other unusual beliefs, just the messages and the watching. It's just so unsettling.
Did your memory or thinking problems begin before you started feeling watched and hearing voices?

Well, no, they all kind of started together. The voices, those messages in the bulletin, and my trouble keeping my thoughts straight... it's all been happening for about eleven months now. 

Eleven months... that means it started right around the time of the county fair last year. Oh, I always used to love the county fair. They have this one booth that sells the most wonderful funnel cakes. You have to get them right when they come out of the fryer, still hot, with just a mountain of powdered sugar on top. Of course, you can't wear black if you're going to eat one, or you'll look like a chalkboard by the time you're done! My daughter wore a black sweater one year, and she was just covered in white dust. We had to take a damp cloth to it in the ladies' room. The ladies' room at the fairgrounds is always so drafty, though. They really need to fix the window in there. It's been stuck open since at least 2015. 

But yes, eleven months of all of this happening.
Have you noticed increasing difficulty remembering recent conversations or events?

Well, I haven't really noticed any trouble with my memory, no. I mean, I can remember just fine what we were talking about earlier, and what I had for breakfast. I had a bowl of oatmeal this morning. I always make it on the stove, never in the microwave. The microwave just makes it all gummy, don't you think? You have to use the old-fashioned rolled oats, not the quick-cooking kind. And I stir in a little bit of brown sugar and a splash of milk. Sometimes I add raisins, but only if they're plump. I bought a box of raisins last week from the new grocery store on Main Street, and they were hard as little pebbles! I almost broke a tooth. That store used to be a roller rink when my daughter was a teenager. She had her thirteenth birthday party there. They played all that loud disco music and served pizza that tasted like cardboard. But the kids just loved it. She wore these bright pink leg warmers... oh, they were something else. 

But no, my memory seems to be working just the way it always has.
Have you had difficulty managing your bills recently?

Well, no, I haven't had any trouble with my bills at all. I always sit down right on the first of the month at my kitchen table and write out all my checks. I still use paper checks, you know. I just don't trust putting all my bank information on the computer. My daughter says I'm being old-fashioned, but you hear such awful stories on the evening news about those hackers. 

Anyway, I write them out and walk them right down to the mailbox. Although, I will say, the price of stamps lately is just getting absolutely ridiculous! I went to the post office last Tuesday to buy a roll of stamps, the post office over on Elm Street. The clerk there, Arthur, he's been working there for years and years. He always wears the most interesting ties. Last week he had on a tie with little yellow ducks all over it. It was just so cute. It reminded me of when I used to take my daughter to the pond at the city park to feed the ducks when she was little. We used to bring leftover bread, but then I read in a magazine in the doctor's waiting room that bread is actually terrible for ducks. It makes them bloated or something, and ruins the water. So we started bringing frozen peas instead. They just gobble them right up. But you have to thaw them a little bit first, otherwise they're too hard for their little beaks. I usually just run them under warm water in a colander. I have this lovely yellow enamel colander I bought at a yard sale back in... oh, it must have been 1998. It has a little chip on the handle, but it works just fine. 

But yes, my bills are all paid up, no problems there.
Are the voices a frequent or ongoing experience for you?

Well, I wouldn't say it's all the time, no. It's mostly just... sometimes, when the house gets really quiet. I'll hear my name, or just a few words, and it sounds exactly like my friend's voice coming from the kitchen or out on the porch. It's so clear that I actually answer back out loud before I remember that nobody is even there. 

My porch is usually a lovely place to sit, though. I did just put up these beautiful new wind chimes out there last week. I found them at a little craft fair over in the next town. They're made of sea glass—mostly blues and greens, just gorgeous when the sun hits them. The woman who made them said she collects the glass herself down at the beach. Oh, I haven't been to the beach in years. My husband and I used to go down to the shore every August. We'd rent this little cottage and just sit outside in the evenings eating salt water taffy. You really have to be careful with salt water taffy, though, because it'll pull a filling right out of your tooth if you aren't paying attention! My dentist, Dr. Henderson, he's always telling me to stay away from the sticky candies. He has this massive aquarium in his waiting room with the most fascinating little neon fish. I could watch them swim around for hours. They dart back and forth so fast, and they have these tiny little glowing stripes on their sides...

My porch is usually a lovely place to sit, though. I did just put up these beautiful new wind chimes out there last week. I found them at a little craft fair over in the next town. They're made of sea glass—mostly blues and greens, just gorgeous when the sun hits them. The woman who made them said she collects the glass herself down at the beach. Oh, I haven't been to the beach in years. My husband and I used to go down to the shore every August. We'd rent this little cottage and just sit outside in the evenings eating salt water taffy. You really have to be careful with salt water taffy, though, because it'll pull a filling right out of your tooth if you aren't paying attention! My dentist, Dr. Henderson, he's always telling me to stay away from the sticky candies. He has this massive aquarium in his waiting room with the most fascinating little neon fish. I could watch them swim around for hours. They dart back and forth so fast, and they have these tiny little glowing stripes on their sides...
